svg.aria-label: Diagram: what Amazon CloudWatch Omni collects and where the resulting data lands. On the left, the observed estate: workloads across all AWS accounts and Regions, plus other clouds including Azure, emitting OpenTelemetry signals, and agent applications emitting every prompt, every model call and every tool invocation. In the centre, the Omni space itself, a standalone web experience entered through single sign-on and available in only three Regions, US East N. Virginia, US West Oregon and Europe Ireland, which automatically discovers services, maps dependencies and surfaces golden metrics, with a free IDE extension for VS Code, Cursor and Kiro as a second entry point. A panel notes the asymmetry that Omni observes every Region and other clouds from three Regions. On the right, the consequence for data: a prompt is whatever the user typed, so agent telemetry contains names, account numbers and medical details as ordinary content rather than as an accident. The control is a CloudWatch Logs data protection policy, which masks matching sensitive data at all egress points including Logs Insights, metric filters and subscription filters, with only holders of the logs:Unmask permission able to see the original. A closing panel records the property that decides everything: masking happens at ingestion, and AWS states that log events ingested before the policy was set are not masked, so there is no retroactive protection and the policy must exist before the telemetry starts.
svg.title: Every prompt is now telemetry, and the control only works forward
svg.text: CloudWatch Omni captures every prompt. A prompt is whatever the user typed.
That is the telemetry an agent needs to be debuggable, and it is also user data arriving in an observability plane.

What it can detect, and why each one matters in a prompt
Credentials · Financial information · Personally Identifiable Information · Protected Health Information · Device identifiers
A support agent is asked about an account. A claims assistant is told a diagnosis. None of that is an accident — it is the input.
The property that decides the ordering
“Sensitive data is detected and masked when it is ingested into the log group. When you set a data
protection policy, log events ingested to the log group before that time are not masked.”
There is no retroactive masking. A policy written after the first fortnight of traces leaves that fortnight in the clear,
and deletion is the only remedy. The policy belongs before the Omni space, not after it.
An account-level policy covers log groups that do not exist yet — the right shape when a new product is about to create them.
LogEventsWithFindings in AWS/Logs is a free vended metric. It is the only signal that sensitive data is arriving at all.
The asymmetry worth noting: Omni observes every Region and other clouds, from three Regions. Residency is the first question.
